key_insight: Routers can be trained without human labels by using synthetic queries and answers generated from high-level task descriptions, enabling annotation-free estimation of each expert LLM's skill for routing decisions.
problem_solved: How to build effective LLM routers when real labeled data is unavailable or user request distributions are heterogeneous and unknown.
method: Use generator LLMs to produce diverse synthetic query–answer pairs from high-level task descriptions (no human annotation).
Train a router on this generated dataset to predict which expert model will perform best on a given input (annotation-free skill estimation).
Validate and calibrate router decisions via proxy signals (e.g., cross-model agreement, confidence scores, or generated evaluation prompts) to improve expert selection under distribution shift.
impact: Enables scalable, low-cost deployment of LLM routing systems without costly annotation pipelines, making model selection robust to diverse and unknown user request distributions.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: Task descriptions → Generator LLM → Synthetic dataset → Router training → Expert selection
Before/after comparison: labeled-data router vs. annotation-free (RGD) router performance and cost (bars or icons)
Sankey or routing flow showing inputs mapped to selected experts with estimated skill scores
Icon set summarizing benefits: lower annotation cost, improved scalability, and robustness to unknown distributions
paper_title: Routing with Generated Data: Annotation-Free LLM Skill Estimation and Expert Selection
paper_authors: Tianyi Niu, Justin Chih-Yao Chen, Genta Indra Winata, Shi-Xiong Zhang, Supriyo Chakraborty
